1	Company Overview
2	Do you already have any cold email templates you’ve used that have worked? Share as many as possible below if so.
3	Outbound so far has been founder-led and mostly warm intros, YC network and industry events, so there is no proven cold template library to hand over. Treat this as a fresh start.
4	Having said that, what converts the fastest is when we show them a demo of the voice agent tailored to their specific company. We can share a link in the follow-up email where they can enter their phone number to get a call from the agent made for their company; it always works.
5	Describe your company briefly, with a Hero Statement. What do you do, for who, and how does it help them?
6	Hero statement: Every property claim burns $60-80 of labor before a single repair begins, most of it an intake team re-keying the same loss into half a dozen systems while the estimate sits in a queue for days. Cozmo replaces that manual layer with an AI workforce that picks up the first call, files the claim, dispatches the crew and delivers a carrier-ready estimate in minutes. Cost per claim drops under $20, cash lands days sooner and storm season stops being a hiring problem. The claim runs itself, and the P&L shows it within the first quarter.
7	The money story by segment:
8	* TPAs and franchise networks: the claims intake operation is a $2-3M a year cost centre, desk estimators add $80-150K a year per location, and 30-40% of dispatches go out in duplicate. Cozmo takes cost per claim from $60-80 to under $20 and turns 3-5 day estimates into minutes. At network scale that is millions a year straight back into EBITDA, which is exactly what a PE owner is asking claims leadership to find.
9	* Restoration contractors: for them, Cozmo is a revenue product. They already pay for every inbound call through ad spend, and every one that rings out is a job the competitor wins. Cozmo answers 100% of calls 24/7 and puts crews on site in 45 minutes on average, so marketing dollars already spent convert into booked jobs, and faster estimates mean the money comes in the same week the water does.
10	* Insurance carriers: the target is loss-adjustment expense. 70% lower cost per successful resolution, revenue-cycle work that took 4-6 hours of human touch time done in about 20 minutes, and structured loss data from the first touch that sharpens every downstream decision from reserves to pricing.
11	The workforce behind those numbers answers the first notice of loss on any channel, files the claim into the systems of record, dispatches the nearest qualified crew and produces the carrier-ready estimate, with every action logged and auditable. It plugs into Xactimate, Symbility, XactAnalysis, the CRM and the phone lines already in place, and deploys in days against live call volume. Over 2 million production calls handled, and 95% of callers never notice they spoke to an AI.
12	What is your product lineup? What offers do you have and how do they differ? Which can we focus on? The more the better.
13	Two products in production, and each one attacks one of the two biggest cost lines in a property claim: the intake operation and the estimation desk.
14	* FNOL Automation. Removes the intake cost centre. Every first notice of loss, on every channel, around the clock, captured, filed into the systems of record and dispatched without a human touching it. At our anchor deployment this replaced work that cost $2-3M a year and cut cost per claim by more than two thirds. Sold to the exec who owns intake spend, after-hours coverage and SLA penalties. In production at volume today.
15	* Estimate Automation. Attacks the single biggest labor line in restoration: desk estimators at $80-150K a year per location, which adds up to $100-200M a year across a large franchise network. Estimates go from 3-5 days to minutes with carrier-ready Xactimate and Symbility language, so revenue gets recognized the same day the photos come in. Rolling out now on a purpose-built estimation model.
16	The value case by segment:
17	* Cozmo for TPAs. PE owners want EBITDA improvement this year, and claims handling is where it hides: manual re-keying across a dozen carrier programs, duplicate dispatches running 30-40% and an intake org that scales only by hiring. Cozmo takes millions out of that cost base in weeks, with throughput per adjuster and cost per claim as the board-level metrics.
18	* Cozmo for Restoration. A revenue machine, priced like a utility. Every call answered, every job captured, crews on site in 45 minutes, estimates out in minutes so cash comes in faster. Native connectors to Encircle, Dash, Albiware and ServiceTitan. Live in about 7 business days, flat monthly fee, no setup fees or per-minute charges.
19	* Cozmo for Carriers. Loss-adjustment expense down 70% per successful resolution, from FNOL through settlement, with policy decisions and core system updates included. Pilot to production in about 3 weeks against existing call volume, so the CFO sees the savings inside a quarter.
20	Under all three sits APE, our Agent Protocol Engine: policy enforcement, deterministic guardrails and an audit trail covering 100% of agent actions. This is what the prospect’s compliance team needs before they sign, so it belongs early in the pitch.
21	Suggested emphasis: our wedge is PE-backed contractor TPAs and independent TPAs. They carry urgent bottom-line pressure and sign fast, where carriers run 18-24 month cycles. Our anchor customer signed a corporate agreement without a POC. Weight the outbound toward TPA and franchise-network corporate leadership, with independent restoration companies as the volume play and carriers as a longer nurture track.
22	What are some unique differentiators vs the competition?
23	* The P&L impact is measured, and large. Cost per claim from $60-80 to under $20. Revenue-cycle work from 4-6 hours of human touch time to about 20 minutes. Estimates from 3-5 days to minutes. At our anchor deployment the savings identified run $4-10M a year and grow with the rollout. Every other differentiator on this list exists to make those numbers credible.
24	* End-to-end ownership of the claim. A Cozmo agent runs the claim from first call to settlement, including decisions and system-of-record updates. Most claims AI stops at intake and hands the rest back to the prospect’s team, which is why it never moves the P&L.
25	* We do the work the incumbents only measure. Verisk and CCC (~$40B combined) became the system of record by owning the measurement standard, and neither one does the work or has field presence. Cozmo runs the connective work from FNOL through estimate, the part no single player owns today.
26	* The loss data compounds. Each claim captures the photos, the scope and the settled amount together, which the system of record never sees in one place. Every claim makes the agents faster and more accurate.
27	* No rip-and-replace. We sit on top of existing systems of record and update them in parallel: Xactimate, Symbility, XactAnalysis, Respond365, Zendesk, CompanyCam, Matterport. Our anchor customer gave us CRM access on a Friday evening and most workflows were automated by Tuesday.
28	* Callers cannot tell. 95% of calls complete without the caller realizing they spoke to an AI. The agent even adapts its accent to the caller’s region. Customer experience holds while the cost drops.
29	* Outcome-based pricing. Carriers and TPAs pay when a case resolves. A failed resolution costs nothing, which removes most of the risk objection in a cold conversation.
30	* Built for a regulated industry. Explainable decisions, deterministic guardrails and a complete audit trail of every action through APE, available on demand for a CISO review. SOC 2 Type 1 complete; Type 2 in its observation window, due October.
31	* Proof of scale. 2M+ production calls at 850ms latency, 43% month-over-month growth, production accounts in 3 countries, local numbers in 80+ countries and 110+ languages with mid-sentence code-switching.
32	* Anchor traction. One of the top 3 contractor TPAs in the US ($2.8B, 1,400+ franchises) runs FNOL and estimate automation from corporate, now rolling out across the franchise network, alongside live carrier deployments in production. No names in outbound until cleared.
33	* Speed to live. 3-week pilot to production for carriers, roughly 7 business days for restoration teams.
34	* Credentials. Y Combinator-backed, San Francisco-based. Alok Kumar (co-founder and CEO) is a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree and runs the forward-deployed commercial model. Nuha Hashem (co-founder and CTO, PMI Future 50) is the architect of APE. The engineering team has shipped at Amazon and led engineering at YC-backed startups.
35	Targeting
36	Locations:
37	United States first, all states. CAT-exposed states (TX, FL, CA, CO, LA and the Gulf and Southeast generally) are the richest territory for both carriers and restoration. Global reach across 80+ countries is a proof point to mention in copy, but do not target outside the US in this first phase.
38	Company headcount range:
39	* Carriers: 200 to 10,000+. Regional and mid-market carriers are the most reachable; national carriers are logo targets for ABM-style sequences.
40	* TPAs and independent adjusting firms: 50 to 1,000.
41	* Restoration contractors: 10 to 200, including franchise operators (Servpro, ServiceMaster, Paul Davis franchisees and similar).
42	Persona job titles:
43	* Carriers: Chief Claims Officer, SVP/VP Claims, Head of Claims Operations, VP Claims Innovation or Claims Transformation, Head of Customer Experience, COO. Secondary technical buyer: CIO/CTO, Head of Digital.
44	* TPAs: CEO, President, COO, VP Operations, Director of Claims, Head of Client Services.
45	* Restoration: Owner, President, General Manager, Operations Manager, Office Manager (often controls the phones).
46	Top Industries:
47	* Property and casualty insurance carriers (personal and commercial lines).
48	* Third-party administrators and independent adjusting firms.
49	* Restoration and mitigation contractors: water, fire, smoke, mold, storm.
50	* Adjacent and worth testing: MGAs/MGUs with claims authority, PE operating partners at firms that own TPA or restoration platforms.
51	Named account targets. Contractor TPAs: Servpro (2,800 locations), Belfor (1,000 franchises), Paul Davis, PuroClean, 911 Restoration. Independent TPAs: Sedgwick, Crawford, Alacrity. The top 100 US contractor networks are PE-backed and control roughly 80% of 75,000 contractors, and about 300 major TPAs process $100B in claims a year, so a focused ABM list beats broad spray at the top of this market.
52	Triggers and Personalisation
53	What job title(s) exist at a company that signal an interest or need for your product and why?
54	At carriers and TPAs: any title containing Claims Transformation, Claims Innovation, Claims Automation or Digital Claims means the company has budget and a mandate for exactly what we sell. Head of FNOL, Head of Claims Intake or claims contact-centre leadership signals the intake pain sits with a named owner. At restoration companies: a dedicated intake coordinator or dispatcher on staff means call volume has outgrown the front desk, which is the moment Cozmo pays for itself.
55	What role(s) might a company be hiring for that signal an interest or need for your product and why?
56	Hiring is the strongest signal we have, because it prices the pain in salary terms.
57	* Carriers/TPAs hiring: FNOL representatives, claims intake specialists, claims call-centre agents, claims assistants, customer service reps in the claims org. Each posting is headcount being added to work Cozmo does. Postings for claims automation, AI or digital claims roles signal an active initiative we should be part of.
58	* Restoration hiring: after-hours answering staff, dispatchers, intake/office coordinators. A company paying for night coverage is a company missing calls today.
59	Is a prospect following a competitor/partner on LinkedIn? What would be the ideal company(s) for them to be following and why?
60	* Claims AI companies: Five Sigma, EvolutionIQ, Roots Automation, Sprout.ai, Liberate. Following any of these means they are watching the claims automation space.
61	* Ecosystem partners: Verisk/Xactimate, CoreLogic/Symbility, Encircle, Albiware, ServiceTitan, Dash. Following these signals they run the systems we connect to natively, which makes the integration story concrete.
62	* Voice AI platforms: following general voice-AI companies suggests they are exploring automated call handling and can be shown a purpose-built alternative.
63	Is a prospect liking/commenting on the content of relevant LinkedIn influencer(s)? Which influencers and why is it relevant?
64	Insurtech commentators are the best proxy for modernization appetite on the carrier/TPA side: Matteo Carbone, Bryan Falchuk (The Future of Insurance), Insurtech Insights, Coverager and Digital Insurance. On the restoration side, engagement with C&R (Cleaning & Restoration) Magazine, KnowHow and restoration business coaches signals an owner investing in how the business runs. Engagement with claims-AI content of any kind is a direct trigger and should be referenced in the first line.
65	Has the prospect listed something on their LinkedIn profile? A relevant qualification, keyword mention in their bio etc
66	* Bio keywords: claims transformation, digital claims, FNOL, claims experience, customer experience, automation, AI, operational excellence.
67	* Designations: CPCU, AIC or SCLA paired with innovation language marks a claims professional who thinks beyond process adherence.
68	* Restoration: IICRC certifications plus language like 24/7 emergency response, which is a promise Cozmo helps them keep.
69	Has the company listed something relevant on their website? A keyword mention, company initiative.
70	* A phone-first "report a claim" page or 24/7 claims hotline: the workflow we automate, visible in public.
71	* Careers pages with open intake, FNOL or call-centre roles.
72	* Press releases or annual reports mentioning claims modernization, digital strategy or customer experience investment.
73	* CAT-readiness or storm-response pages, which imply seasonal call surges their team cannot staff for.
74	* Restoration sites promising "we answer 24/7" or "on site in 60 minutes": we let them keep that promise and can beat it (45-minute average).
75	Is the company engaged in any other relevant activity? E.g running meta ads, listed on a specific directory, announcing a new product launch etc.
76	* Restoration companies running Google Local Service or Meta ads are paying per call, and every missed call is wasted ad spend. Sharp personalisation angle.
77	* TPAs announcing new carrier programs or contract wins: volume is about to spike ahead of headcount.
78	* Exhibiting or speaking at PLRB, RIA Convention, ClaimsX, ITC (InsureTech Connect) or Insurtech Insights.
79	* A recent CAT event in their operating region: both carriers and restoration firms are drowning in calls in the following weeks.
80	* Poor Google reviews mentioning missed calls, slow callbacks or unreachable adjusters.
81	* A PE acquisition of a TPA or restoration platform. New PE owners arrive with a cost-cutting mandate, and a slow storm season has them looking at claims-handling spend line by line. This is the single best-timed moment to reach them.
82	Is the company using relevant technology? This could be a competitor or complimentary technology. Why is it relevant?
83	* Encircle, Dash, Albiware or ServiceTitan: we have native connectors, so the pitch becomes "live in your existing stack in about a week".
84	* Xactimate or Symbility: we output carrier-ready scope language for both.
85	* Guidewire, Duck Creek or similar core systems: complementary. We update these systems rather than compete with them.
86	* Answering services or basic IVRs: the incumbent we replace. An answering service takes a message; Cozmo resolves the claim.
87	* A competitor intake bot: they have validated the budget line and can be moved with the end-to-end and outcome-pricing story.
88	Feel free to list any other signals you think might be relevant.
89	* Hurricane and wildfire season timing by region. Sequences to CAT-exposed states should land before the season, when readiness is on the agenda.
90	* J.D. Power claims satisfaction rankings: carriers near the bottom have a public, board-visible problem.
91	* State DOI complaint data referencing claims delays or communication failures.
92	* Spanish-speaking market concentration: carriers and contractors serving TX, FL, CA and the Southwest respond well to the native-quality Spanish and code-switching capability.
93	* Soft-market pressure: carriers publicly discussing expense ratios or claims cost reduction in earnings calls and rate filings are under board-level pressure to cut cost per claim now. That commentary is a first-line personalisation angle.
94	Case Studies
95	Please list as many case studies as possible we can use. Include the name of the company and the results achieved where possible.
96	Deployments we can talk about today (no names in outbound copy):
97	* One of the top 3 contractor TPAs in the US ($2.8B, 1,400+ franchises across the US and Canada) signed a corporate agreement without a POC and went live two months ahead of the target. Their previous AI provider spent 8 months and never launched; our team replicated the workflow in two days on site. Manual intake ran 20 minutes per claim across 250-1,000 claims a day, with claims arriving by email from 13+ carriers in inconsistent formats.
98	* Cozmo now handles intake, entry into the systems of record and franchisee dispatch with a 15-minute SLA and auto-reassignment. Their Zendesk layer was retired within two weeks, corporate is rolling the product out across the franchise network, and leadership has asked for 7 workflows beyond the original 3.
99	Allianz Insurance and Discovery Insurance: live carrier deployments from our financial services work.
100	Platform-level proof points, public on the website and safe in any copy:
101	* 2M+ production calls handled, in Spanish, English, Hindi, Arabic and 110+ languages.
102	* 70% lower cost per successful resolution for carriers.
103	* 45-minute average crew on-site response for restoration deployments.
104	* 3 weeks from pilot to production for carrier deployments; about 7 business days to live for restoration teams.
105	* 100% of agent actions captured with an audit trail.
106	* In live production with carriers, TPAs and restoration companies today.
107	Offers and Lead Magnets
108	Can we offer prospects a free trial (if applicable)?
109	There is no standing free trial, but once certain volumes are hit for larger carriers and TPAs, they pay only when a claim is filed and settled, so they eventually carry no cost until Cozmo delivers.
110	Small restoration companies have no setup fees. Frame it as "run a pilot against your live call volume; if a case doesn’t resolve, you don’t pay."
111	Can we offer to send a video walkthrough of our product/service (if applicable)? What videos and why?
112	Yes, but only offer it if they respond and are specifically interested in seeing the platform. We prefer to give the demo live; even a 15-minute meeting is sufficient.
113	Do we have any downloadable resources to offer? (e.g. whitepapers, templates, reports)
114	Nothing packaged for download yet. Quick wins we can produce: a one-pager per segment, a cost-per-resolved-claim benchmark sheet for carriers/TPAs and a missed-call revenue calculator for restoration owners.
115	Can we invite them to a live webinar, in-person event, or recorded masterclass?
116	We can, but we would have to create it if we get enough interest; nothing is planned as of now. A recorded masterclass built from demo footage (for example, "watch an AI agent take a claim from first call to filed FNOL in 12 minutes") is realistic within a few weeks if the sequences need it. We do attend industry events and can invite prospects to meet there.
117	Can we offer to meet them in person?
118	Yes, selectively. We are San Francisco-based and travel for carrier and TPA deals, and we are flexible depending on the logo size. Industry events (ITC, PLRB, RIA, ClaimsX) are the natural venue for in-person meetings and a good CTA in the weeks before each one.
119	Can we offer a free audit, strategy call, or consultation?
120	Yes, and this is our best offer: a live demo where the Cozmo agent calls the prospect and takes a mock loss report from them on the spot, in English, Spanish or the language of their choice. We run this live in investor and customer meetings and the agent collects a full FNOL (name, address, damage type, scope) in about two minutes. It requires nothing from their IT team and sells better than any deck. We can also run a claims-intake cost analysis from their call volume and average handle time.
121	Can we offer part of our service for free? E.g. A free landing page, free branding concepts, first hire for free etc
122	The live-call demo is effectively a free sample of the product. For restoration, an after-hours overflow line is a plausible low-friction entry offer.
123	Anything else we can offer to prospects to entice them to respond?
124	* The agent-calls-you demo, personalised: the agent can greet them by name and reference their company. Memorable and shareable internally.
125	* For multilingual books of business: a demo call in Spanish, Arabic, Hindi or Portuguese.
126	* Speed framing as an offer: "live in 7 business days" (restoration) and "pilot to production in 3 weeks" (carriers) counter the assumption that this is a year-long IT project.
127	Additional Info
128	Please add any other details or insights not covered above that could help us shape a stronger strategy.
129	* Copy speaks in money, always. C-suite prospects buy cost per claim down 70%, an intake cost centre removed, estimator spend eliminated and revenue landing days sooner. What the agents do is the proof behind those claims, never the headline. If a first line describes a feature instead of a dollar outcome, rewrite it.
130	* Lead with the demo, always. The single best conversion moment we have is the prospect experiencing the agent on a live call. Every sequence should drive to that, and copy should describe it concretely ("our agent will call you and take a claim") rather than offering "a demo".
131	* Positioning guardrail. Never pitch Cozmo as a chatbot, an answering service or a general voice-AI tool. The category is an AI claims workforce that owns the case end to end. This matters most with carrier buyers, who have seen intake bots and been unimpressed.
132	* Compliance is a selling point, so use it early. Explainable decisions, deterministic guardrails and the 100% audit trail belong in carrier and TPA messaging from the first touch. It pre-empts the objection that kills most AI conversations in insurance.
133	* Objection to expect: "we tried an AI provider". Our anchor customer had one that spent 8 months without launching; we replicated the workflow in two days on site and went live two months early. Company Overview
Do you already have any cold email templates you’ve used that have worked? Share as many as possible below if so.
Outbound so far has been founder-led and mostly warm intros, YC network and industry events, so there is no proven cold template library to hand over. Treat this as a fresh start.
Having said that, what converts the fastest is when we show them a demo of the voice agent tailored to their specific company. We can share a link in the follow-up email where they can enter their phone number to get a call from the agent made for their company; it always works.
Describe your company briefly, with a Hero Statement. What do you do, for who, and how does it help them?
Hero statement: Every property claim burns $60-80 of labor before a single repair begins, most of it an intake team re-keying the same loss into half a dozen systems while the estimate sits in a queue for days. Cozmo replaces that manual layer with an AI workforce that picks up the first call, files the claim, dispatches the crew and delivers a carrier-ready estimate in minutes. Cost per claim drops under $20, cash lands days sooner and storm season stops being a hiring problem. The claim runs itself, and the P&L shows it within the first quarter.
The money story by segment:
* TPAs and franchise networks: the claims intake operation is a $2-3M a year cost centre, desk estimators add $80-150K a year per location, and 30-40% of dispatches go out in duplicate. Cozmo takes cost per claim from $60-80 to under $20 and turns 3-5 day estimates into minutes. At network scale that is millions a year straight back into EBITDA, which is exactly what a PE owner is asking claims leadership to find.
* Restoration contractors: for them, Cozmo is a revenue product. They already pay for every inbound call through ad spend, and every one that rings out is a job the competitor wins. Cozmo answers 100% of calls 24/7 and puts crews on site in 45 minutes on average, so marketing dollars already spent convert into booked jobs, and faster estimates mean the money comes in the same week the water does.
* Insurance carriers: the target is loss-adjustment expense. 70% lower cost per successful resolution, revenue-cycle work that took 4-6 hours of human touch time done in about 20 minutes, and structured loss data from the first touch that sharpens every downstream decision from reserves to pricing.
The workforce behind those numbers answers the first notice of loss on any channel, files the claim into the systems of record, dispatches the nearest qualified crew and produces the carrier-ready estimate, with every action logged and auditable. It plugs into Xactimate, Symbility, XactAnalysis, the CRM and the phone lines already in place, and deploys in days against live call volume. Over 2 million production calls handled, and 95% of callers never notice they spoke to an AI.
What is your product lineup? What offers do you have and how do they differ? Which can we focus on? The more the better.
Two products in production, and each one attacks one of the two biggest cost lines in a property claim: the intake operation and the estimation desk.
* FNOL Automation. Removes the intake cost centre. Every first notice of loss, on every channel, around the clock, captured, filed into the systems of record and dispatched without a human touching it. At our anchor deployment this replaced work that cost $2-3M a year and cut cost per claim by more than two thirds. Sold to the exec who owns intake spend, after-hours coverage and SLA penalties. In production at volume today.
* Estimate Automation. Attacks the single biggest labor line in restoration: desk estimators at $80-150K a year per location, which adds up to $100-200M a year across a large franchise network. Estimates go from 3-5 days to minutes with carrier-ready Xactimate and Symbility language, so revenue gets recognized the same day the photos come in. Rolling out now on a purpose-built estimation model.
The value case by segment:
* Cozmo for TPAs. PE owners want EBITDA improvement this year, and claims handling is where it hides: manual re-keying across a dozen carrier programs, duplicate dispatches running 30-40% and an intake org that scales only by hiring. Cozmo takes millions out of that cost base in weeks, with throughput per adjuster and cost per claim as the board-level metrics.
* Cozmo for Restoration. A revenue machine, priced like a utility. Every call answered, every job captured, crews on site in 45 minutes, estimates out in minutes so cash comes in faster. Native connectors to Encircle, Dash, Albiware and ServiceTitan. Live in about 7 business days, flat monthly fee, no setup fees or per-minute charges.
* Cozmo for Carriers. Loss-adjustment expense down 70% per successful resolution, from FNOL through settlement, with policy decisions and core system updates included. Pilot to production in about 3 weeks against existing call volume, so the CFO sees the savings inside a quarter.
Under all three sits APE, our Agent Protocol Engine: policy enforcement, deterministic guardrails and an audit trail covering 100% of agent actions. This is what the prospect’s compliance team needs before they sign, so it belongs early in the pitch.
Suggested emphasis: our wedge is PE-backed contractor TPAs and independent TPAs. They carry urgent bottom-line pressure and sign fast, where carriers run 18-24 month cycles. Our anchor customer signed a corporate agreement without a POC. Weight the outbound toward TPA and franchise-network corporate leadership, with independent restoration companies as the volume play and carriers as a longer nurture track.
What are some unique differentiators vs the competition?
* The P&L impact is measured, and large. Cost per claim from $60-80 to under $20. Revenue-cycle work from 4-6 hours of human touch time to about 20 minutes. Estimates from 3-5 days to minutes. * Built for a regulated industry. Explainable decisions, deterministic guardrails and a complete audit trail of every action through APE, available on demand for a CISO review. SOC 2 Type 1 complete; Type 2 in its observation window, due October.
* Proof of scale. 2M+ production calls at 850ms latency, 43% month-over-month growth, production accounts in 3 countries, local numbers in 80+ countries and 110+ languages with mid-sentence code-switching.
* Anchor traction. One of the top 3 contractor TPAs in the US ($2.8B, 1,400+ franchises) runs FNOL and estimate automation from corporate, now rolling out across the franchise network, alongside live carrier deployments in production. No names in outbound until cleared.
* Speed to live. 3-week pilot to production for carriers, roughly 7 business days for restoration teams.
* Credentials. Y Combinator-backed, San Francisco-based. Alok Kumar (co-founder and CEO) is a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree and runs the forward-deployed commercial model. Nuha Hashem (co-founder and CTO, PMI Future 50) is the architect of APE. The engineering team has shipped at Amazon and led engineering at YC-backed startups.

Locations:
United States first, all states. CAT-exposed states (TX, FL, CA, CO, LA and the Gulf and Southeast generally) are the richest territory for both carriers and restoration. Global reach across 80+ countries is a proof point to mention in copy, but do not target outside the US in this first phase.

* Restoration contractors: 10 to 200, including franchise operators (Servpro, ServiceMaster, Paul Davis franchisees and similar).

* TPAs: CEO, President, COO, VP Operations, Director of Claims, Head of Client Services.
* Restoration: Owner, President, General Manager, Operations Manager, Office Manager (often controls the phones).
Top Industries:

What job title(s) exist at a company that signal an interest or need for your product and why?

Head of FNOL, Head of Claims Intake or claims contact-centre leadership signals the intake pain sits with a named owner. At restoration companies: a dedicated intake coordinator or dispatcher on staff means call volume has outgrown the front desk, which is the moment Cozmo pays for itself.
What role(s) might a company be hiring for that signal an interest or need for your product and why?
Hiring is the strongest signal we have, because it prices the pain in salary terms.
* Carriers/TPAs hiring: FNOL representatives, claims intake specialists, claims call-centre agents, claims assistants, customer service reps in the claims org. * Restoration hiring: after-hours answering staff, dispatchers, intake/office coordinators. A company paying for night coverage is a company missing calls today.
Is a prospect following a competitor/partner on LinkedIn? What would be the ideal company(s) for them to be following and why?
* Claims AI companies: Five Sigma, EvolutionIQ, Roots Automation, Sprout.ai, Liberate. Following any of these means they are watching the claims automation space.
* Ecosystem partners: Verisk/Xactimate, CoreLogic/Symbility, Encircle, Albiware, ServiceTitan, Dash. Following these signals they run the systems we connect to natively, which makes the integration story concrete.
* Voice AI platforms: following general voice-AI companies suggests they are exploring automated call handling and can be shown a purpose-built alternative.

* Restoration: IICRC certifications plus language like 24/7 emergency response, which is a promise Cozmo helps them keep.

# Offer Facts — the DM/outreach agent's fact base

> Compiled 2026-07-22 from Alok's GTM doc (`alok-gtm-doc-2026-07-22.md`, canonical where it conflicts with older sources) + site scrape + onboarding call. **Load this before ANY Cozmo outbound artifact (DM, comment, email, landing copy).** The intake voice questionnaire was NOT completed — this doc supersedes most of it; remaining open items at bottom.

## THE FIVE BINDING RULES (his own words, non-negotiable)
1. **Copy speaks in money, always.** Dollar outcome first, feature as proof. "If a first line describes a feature instead of a dollar outcome, rewrite it."
2. **Lead with the demo, always.** The conversion moment = the agent calling THEM live. Describe it concretely ("our agent will call you and take a claim") — never a vague "demo."
3. **Never pitch as** a chatbot, answering service, or general voice-AI. Category = **"AI claims workforce that owns the case end to end."**
4. **No numbers in outbound pricing.** Safe phrases: outcome-based, priced per claim, pay on resolution, no setup fees (restoration), flat monthly fee by call volume. NEVER the $1–4K, $50–60K, $500→$60, $60-80→<$20 figures in written outbound.
5. **No customer names in outbound** until cleared (anchor TPA, Allianz, Discovery included). No contract values. Nothing about fundraise, ever. Internal-deck numbers need their sign-off before landing in copy.

## The offer (two products)
- **FNOL Automation** — removes the intake cost centre. Every first notice of loss, every channel, 24/7, captured → filed into systems of record → dispatched, no human touch. Sold to the exec who owns intake spend/after-hours/SLA penalties. In production at volume.
- **Estimate Automation** — attacks the desk-estimator line ($80–150K/yr per location; $100–200M/yr across a big network). Estimates 3–5 days → minutes, carrier-ready Xactimate/Symbility language. Rolling out on a purpose-built estimation model.

## Money story per segment (the DM discovery → hook mapping)
- **TPAs/franchise networks (THE WEDGE — PE-backed, sign fast):** intake ops = $2–3M/yr cost centre; duplicate dispatches 30–40%; cost/claim cut by two-thirds+; millions back into EBITDA — "exactly what a PE owner is asking claims leadership to find." Board metrics: throughput per adjuster, cost per claim.
- **Restoration (volume play):** a REVENUE product — they pay for calls via ad spend; every ring-out = a competitor's job. 100% answered 24/7, crews on site 45-min avg, estimates in minutes = cash same week. Live ~7 business days. Utility pricing.
- **Carriers (18–24-mo cycles — nurture track):** loss-adjustment expense down 70%/successful resolution; 4–6 hrs of touch time → ~20 min; structured loss data sharpens reserves→pricing. Pilot→production 3 weeks.

## Proof points (PUBLIC = safe in any copy)
2M+ production calls · 110+ languages, mid-sentence code-switching · 70% lower cost per successful resolution (carriers) · 45-min avg crew response · 3-wk pilot→production / ~7 business days restoration · 100% of actions audit-trailed · 850ms latency · live with carriers, TPAs and restoration companies today.

## Proof points (INTERNAL — check with Cozmo before using in copy)
95% of callers never notice it's AI · 43% MoM growth · production in 3 countries · anchor story details · per-claim economics · savings identified $4–10M/yr at anchor.

## The anchor story (approved anonymous phrasing, no name)
"One of the top 3 contractor TPAs in the US ($2.8B, 1,400+ franchises across the US and Canada) signed a corporate agreement without a POC. Their previous AI provider spent 8 months and never launched; our team replicated the workflow in two days on site. Manual intake was 20 minutes per claim across 250–1,000 claims/day from 13+ carriers. Cozmo now runs intake, system entry and franchisee dispatch on a 15-minute SLA; their Zendesk layer was retired within two weeks; corporate asked for 7 more workflows and is rolling it across the network." *(Doc-sourced; treat as internal-deck material — confirm before written outbound; ideal for Alok's voice on calls + LinkedIn content once cleared.)*
Other deployments: Allianz + Discovery Insurance (carrier deployments from FSI era) — names NOT for outbound.

## Objection playbook (his own answers)
- **"We tried an AI provider."** → The anchor story: 8 months and never launched vs replicated in 2 days on site, live 2 months early. "Intake bots take messages. Cozmo makes decisions, updates the systems of record and closes cases, priced on resolution."
- **Security review.** → SOC 2 **Type 1 complete; Type 2 in observation window, due October**; 100% audit trail a CISO can pull on demand. Put it in the FIRST reply — "keeps deals out of the procurement swamp."
- **"We already have an answering service."** → An answering service takes a message; Cozmo resolves the claim. (Positioning rule #3.)
- **Risk objection generally** → outcome pricing: "run a pilot against your live call volume; if a case doesn't resolve, you don't pay." No standing free trial; restoration has no setup fees.
- **"Year-long IT project" assumption** → live in 7 business days (restoration), 3-week pilot→production (carriers); "CRM access on a Friday evening, most workflows automated by Tuesday."

## The CTA ladder
1. **Best offer: the personalized agent-calls-you demo** — greets them by name, references their company, takes a mock loss report in ~2 min, any language (Spanish/Arabic/Hindi/Portuguese angle for multilingual books). Requires nothing from IT.
2. 15-minute meeting is sufficient (they prefer live demo over video).
3. Video walkthrough only if specifically requested. In-person selectively (they fly for carrier/TPA logos; events: ITC, PLRB, RIA, ClaimsX).
4. Buildable lead magnets (not yet made): segment one-pagers, cost-per-resolved-claim benchmark sheet, missed-call revenue calculator (restoration).

## Targeting (US-only this phase; CAT states richest: TX/FL/CA/CO/LA/Gulf/Southeast)
- **Personas** — Carriers: Chief Claims Officer, SVP/VP Claims, Head of Claims Ops, VP Claims Innovation/Transformation, COO (CIO/CTO secondary-technical). TPAs: CEO, President, COO, VP Ops, Director of Claims, Head of Client Services. Restoration: Owner, President, GM, Ops Manager, **Office Manager (often controls the phones)**.
- **Sizes** — carriers 200–10K+; TPAs/IA firms 50–1,000; restoration 10–200 incl. franchise operators.
- **Champion vs buyer:** transformation/innovation titles = champions to arm with ROI; CCO/COO signs. Cold-pitch the champion, not the signer.
- **Sender split:** Alok (CEO, Forbes 30u30) → commercial personas; Nuha (CTO, PMI Future 50) → technical personas.
- Market frame: ~300 major TPAs process $100B/yr; top 100 contractor networks (PE-backed) control ~80% of 75K contractors. ABM > spray.

## Trigger/signal playbook (for DM personalization + list building)
- **Hiring = strongest signal:** FNOL reps, claims intake, claims call-centre, after-hours answering staff, dispatchers ("a company paying for night coverage is a company missing calls today"). Claims-automation/AI role postings = active initiative.
- **Titles that signal budget:** anything with Claims Transformation/Innovation/Automation/Digital Claims; Head of FNOL/Intake.
- **Tech stack:** Encircle/Dash/Albiware/ServiceTitan = native-connector pitch ("live in your stack in about a week"). Xactimate/Symbility = output-compatible. Guidewire/Duck Creek = complementary. Answering service/IVR = the incumbent. Competitor intake bot = validated budget, move with end-to-end + outcome pricing.
- **Moments:** PE acquisition of a TPA/restoration platform = *the single best-timed moment* (cost-cutting mandate). New carrier-program wins (volume spike ahead of headcount). CAT event in region (good for restoration outreach after; BAD for carriers — they're underwater; hit carriers pre-season). Soft-market expense-ratio talk in earnings calls. Bottom of J.D. Power claims rankings. DOI complaint data on delays. Google reviews mentioning missed calls. Restoration running Google Local Service/Meta ads (paying per call → missed call = wasted ad spend).
- **Watering holes:** Matteo Carbone, Bryan Falchuk, Insurtech Insights, Coverager, Digital Insurance (carrier/TPA side); C&R Magazine, KnowHow, restoration coaches (restoration side). Engagement with any claims-AI content = direct trigger, reference it in line one.
- **Named accounts:** Servpro (2,800 locations), Belfor (1,000), Paul Davis, PuroClean, 911 Restoration; TPAs: Sedgwick, Crawford, Alacrity. (Cross-check tier/disqualifier flags in `targets/dream200-scored.csv`.)
- **Why-now for copy:** agents only recently became capable of end-to-end claims + soft market forcing cost out NOW.

## Known contradictions (resolved: GTM doc wins)
- Can't-tell rate: call said 85–90% → doc says **95%** (internal; site-safe version: "most callers never notice").
- Cost per claim: call's "$500→$60" vs doc's "intake $60–80→under $20" — different scopes; BOTH are no-outbound numbers now anyway. Public version: "70% lower cost per successful resolution."
- Cold email: no proven templates exist; fresh start; demo-link follow-up "always works."

## STILL OPEN (ask casually on WhatsApp; low urgency)
1. Competitor spelling (the garbled "Fatality" — note: doc names Five Sigma, EvolutionIQ, Roots Automation, Sprout.ai, Liberate as claims-AI cos, and calls Verisk+CCC the measurement incumbents; none sound like "Fatality").
2. Do-not-DM list beyond Eberl.
3. Reference calls: offerable, via whom?
4. Follow-up cap + spacing for the DM agent.
5. Commercial large-loss + auto claims: in or out of scope.
6. Outbound sales calls for restoration clients: offered or intake-only.
7. Approved phrase for the anchor TPA in WRITTEN outbound (the $2.8B/1,400-franchise description is doc-internal — confirm it's cleared for DMs).

**Two scenarios, and the honest difference:**

| | Same Mac, new Claude MAX login | Different machine / teammate |
|---|---|---|
| Vault + Snowball files (incl. charts, offer-facts, transcripts) | ✅ all there | ✅ **once committed + pushed** to git |
| Auto-memory (`~/.claude/.../memory/`) | ✅ loads automatically | ⚠️ **NOT in git — machine-local, won't transfer** |
| Vercel app + EC2 logger | ✅ separate infra | ✅ separate infra |
